#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from PBS
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 64 -n 1024 -c 1 -t 1h --job-name=select_neurotrees --output=./results/neurotrees_select-{{id}}.out --error=./results/neurotrees_select-{{id}}.err script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 64        : 64 nodes (from nodes=64)
# -n 1024      : 1024 tasks (from aprun -n 1024; also matches 64 nodes × 16 ppn)
# -c 1         : 1 core per task (implicit from ppn=16 with 1024 tasks)
# -t 1h        : 1 hour walltime (from walltime=1:00:00)
# --job-name=select_neurotrees : job name (from -N select_neurotrees)
# --output=./results/neurotrees_select-{{id}}.out : stdout file with job ID
# --error=./results/neurotrees_select-{{id}}.err : stderr file with job ID
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} or {{jobid}} for job ID instead of $PBS_JOBID

# Original PBS nodes specification: nodes=64:ppn=16:xe
# Breakdown:
# - nodes=64: 64 compute nodes
# - ppn=16: 16 processors per node (64 × 16 = 1024 total)
# - xe: Cray XE node type specification
#
# Flux equivalent:
# -N 64: 64 nodes
# -n 1024: 1024 tasks total (matching aprun -n 1024)
# -c 1: 1 core per task
#
# Note: xe is a PBS node property for Cray XE architecture
# Flux handles node properties through resource constraints
# If specific node types are required, consult site-specific Flux configuration:
# - May use --requires or --setattr for node properties
# - Example: --requires="xe" (if configured in Flux resource graph)
# Performance impact: Job may be scheduled on different node types if not specified

# Original PBS queue: high
# PBS: -q high
# Note: Flux does not have queues in the same way as PBS
# Queue selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling priority depends on site-specific Flux configuration
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or priority settings

# Original PBS walltime: 1:00:00 (1 hour)
# Flux: -t 1h or -t 60m or -t 3600s

# Original PBS job name: select_neurotrees
# Flux: --job-name=select_neurotrees

# Original PBS output/error files:
# PBS: -e ./results/neurotrees_select.$PBS_JOBID.err
# PBS: -o ./results/neurotrees_select.$PBS_JOBID.out
# Flux: --output=./results/neurotrees_select-{{id}}.out
# Flux: --error=./results/neurotrees_select-{{id}}.err
# Note: Flux uses {{id}}, {{jobid}}, or {{name}} for substitutions
# Changed delimiter from '.' to '-' for clarity

# Email notification (commented out in original):
# PBS: ##PBS -m bea (begin, end, abort)
# Note: Flux does not have built-in email notification directives
# Performance impact: User must manually monitor job status or implement external
# monitoring solutions using flux job events, flux watch commands, or wrapper scripts

# Umask setting:
# PBS: -W umask=0027
# Note: Flux does not have a direct umask directive
# Set umask in the script itself (done below)
# Performance impact: No functional impact, umask is set in script
umask 0027

# Module environment
module swap PrgEnv-cray PrgEnv-gnu
module load cray-hdf5-parallel

set -x

# Working directory
# PBS: $PBS_O_WORKDIR (submission directory)
# Flux: $FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR or use --cwd flag at submission
cd ${FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR:-$PWD}

# Execute application
# PBS: aprun -n 1024 (Cray-specific MPI launcher)
# Flux: Use flux run to launch MPI tasks
# aprun is Cray's application launcher, similar to mpirun/mpiexec
# Flux equivalent: flux run -n 1024
#
# Note: aprun options translation:
# -n 1024: 1024 MPI tasks → flux run -n 1024
# aprun has many options for task placement, binding, etc.
# For basic execution, flux run -n <tasks> is sufficient
# For advanced placement/binding, consult Flux documentation
flux run -n 1024 ./build/neurotrees_select -p GC -i 256 --reindex \
      --cachesize=$((4 * 1024 * 1024)) \
      /projects/sciteam/baef/Full_Scale_Control/DGC_forest_extended_20171019_compressed.h5 \
      /projects/sciteam/baef/Full_Scale_Control/DGC_forest_reindex_20170615.dat \
      /projects/sciteam/baef/Full_Scale_Control/DGC_forest_20171019.h5

# Note on execution:
# Original used aprun (Cray Application Level Placement Scheduler)
# Flux uses flux run for launching parallel applications
# Both distribute MPI tasks across allocated nodes
# With -N 64 -n 1024, Flux will distribute 1024 tasks across 64 nodes
# (approximately 16 tasks per node, matching original ppn=16)

# Complete submission command:
# flux batch -N 64 -n 1024 -c 1 -t 1h \
#   --job-name=select_neurotrees \
#   --output=./results/neurotrees_select-{{id}}.out \
#   --error=./results/neurotrees_select-{{id}}.err \
#   script.sh
#
# Ensure ./results/ directory exists before submission:
# mkdir -p ./results

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts PBS directives to Flux command-line options.
Resource calculations are accurate: 64 nodes × 16 tasks/node = 1024 total tasks, matching the flux run command.
The flux run command specifies '-n 1024' which matches the batch allocation of '-n 1024', ensuring all allocated tasks are used.

However, the output/error file placeholders use '{{id}}' which should be verified. Flux typically uses '{{id}}' or '{{jobid}}' for job ID substitution, but the actual syntax may vary by Flux version. Test with a simple job to confirm the correct placeholder format.

The script uses relative paths for output files ('./results/neurotrees_select-{{id}}.out'). The submission command should either use '--cwd' flag to set working directory, or the paths should be absolute to ensure files are written to the intended location.

The working directory handling uses '${FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR:-$PWD}' as a fallback. This is good practice, but verify that FLUX_JOB_SUBMITDIR is the correct environment variable for your Flux version (it may be FLUX_SUBMIT_DIR or similar).

Memory specification is not included. The original PBS script did not specify memory requirements either, but for a job using 1024 tasks, explicit memory allocation per task or per node might be beneficial. Consider adding memory specifications if the application has known requirements.

The Cray XE node type constraint ('xe' from PBS) is documented but not translated to Flux. If specific node architectures are required, investigate '--requires' or '--setattr' options for your Flux instance to ensure the job runs on compatible nodes.

The 'high' queue priority from PBS is not translated. If job priority is important, investigate Flux's job priority mechanisms (e.g., '--setattr=system.priority=<value>' or similar site-specific options).

The cores-per-task specification (-c 1) assumes 1 core per task. With 1024 tasks on 64 nodes, this gives 16 tasks per node. Verify that nodes have at least 16 cores and that the application's threading model matches this configuration.

The script does not validate that the './results/' directory exists before submission. The submission notes mention 'mkdir -p ./results' but this is not included in the script itself. Consider adding this check to the script.
The Cray-specific modules (PrgEnv-gnu, cray-hdf5-parallel) may not be available in all Flux environments. Verify module availability before job submission.

### set the wallclock time

### set the job name

### set the job stdout and stderr
#PBS -e ./results/neurotrees_select.$PBS_JOBID.err

### set email notification
##PBS -m bea
### Set umask so users in my group can read job stdout and stderr files
#PBS -W umask=0027

module load cray-hdf5-parallel

set -x

cd $PBS_O_WORKDIR

aprun -n 1024 ./build/neurotrees_select -p GC -i 256 --reindex \
